en: (Urk. Not the start I was hoping for. I don't know anything about his reputation, but I need to ride this out.)
Well? What have you heard about me?
I heard you're a noble and dignified employer who deeply cares for his workers.

Oh? Haha, I see. Well, I certainly do recognize that quality
in myself, if I may be allowed to boast!
If that really is your motive for seeking work under me, I couldn't be more pleased.
(Bingo. That was the right answer!)

I value each one of our workers like a priceless sculpture⑬
treasures to be cherished and admired. I dedicate my life to
keeping them safe at my bosom. Perhaps you could join them.
I would be honored to, sir!
(Didn't expect things to go this good... Guess it never hurts to try.)
I heard that you're a sharp businessman with a shrewd sense of judgment.
Oh? Haha, I see. Well, I certainly do recognize that quality in myself, if I may be allowed to boast.
If that really is your motive for seeking work under me, I'll have to redouble my efforts!
Oh, no, that isn't⑬

I founded this company on sweat, tears, and more sweat...
Getting where I am today took many a long, hard decision. So
I hope I make the right call regarding whether to hire you.
Yes, I hope so too, sir!
(Oh, yeah. Looking good. This job's in the bag!)
I heard you have a cheerful and fun personality.
Oh? Then having actually met me, what's your personal opinion?
I'm having a great time talking with you, sir!
Haha, then I'm honored. Even if it were just a passing compliment, I feel quite pleased.
Oh, no, no. It wasn't just a compliment⑬I meant it, seriously.
Well, I'll know soon enough whether you're a fulsome fountain or a straight shooter. That's what this interview will tell me.
Then I'm looking forward to speaking with you further, sir!
(I guess this is going pretty good. Don't think I've messed things up too badly yet.)
"I've always dreamed of working in food processing." Really? You're a nightlife journalist, aren't you? That's in an entirely different field.
(Urk. Not the start I was hoping for. That was a dumb thing to write.)
Well? Was it really your dream to work in the food processing industry?
Absolutely, it's true! Food is fundamental to our lives, so I hope to contribute to society's well-being by working in this vital industry.

Oh? Haha, smartly played. You weaseled your way out of that
with a safely vague platitude.
Oh, no, I...
(No way. He took it positively? I guess it doesn't hurt to make shit up sometimes.)
I'm sorry! I lied! I don't know a thing about the food processing industry!

Oh? Well, that's very honest of you to come clean,
especially after I put you on the spot like that.
You seem to be a trustworthy man.
Oh, uh... Thank you.

Now, Shinada, I know you're from Tokyo, but I see you've
lived in Nagoya for quite a long time. Have you always been
a nightlife journalist?
Well, yes... I've managed to scrape by so far.

Indeed. I imagine your income might be unsteady, stringing
along one writing gig to the next. Seems like it could be
quite rough. Perhaps you're ready to move on from that?
Oh, yes, absolutely. I've had enough.
Which is why you came to this interview. That said, you learned of us because you're in the nightlife industry seeking other opportunities.
Perhaps your career of choice was all in preparation for coming to us today.
Maybe I'm blowing things out of proportion, but this could be considered fate, of sorts.
I see. That is a possibility!
(Bring it home, baby! The job's as good as mine!)
With all due respect, I take pride in my work. And I try to live life without regretting the paths I've walked!
Well! Now that takes a lot of heart to say. I like the cut of your jib, son. You've got spunk, much more than I originally thought.
Strawberry's manager must have sent you to me because he saw that quality in you. I need to thank him for that.
I need to thank him, too! It's because of him that I got to meet you, sir!
Haha. You don't miss a beat. You sure know how to please an old man.
Oh no, I'm not that... pleasing.
Not at all! I've always enjoyed being a writer, especially about nightlife. It let me see the true nature of people and shaped who I am today.
Ah, so you're saying work isn't only about the money? It's rare to hear those words coming out sincerely. You have an excellent outlook on life.
But I'm sure you will find our work to be worthwhile, too. I would love for you to experience it.
Thank you, so would I!
Huh? What is on this résumé...? Hrm. What you wrote under your hobbies and skills is quite... intriguing.
It is?
It says, and I quote: "Knocking balls out the park. I'm a home run hammering machine!" Would you care to elaborate?
Ah, that's just baseball talk. I train regularly at the batting center, see.
Hmm, you certainly do have an impressive build, what with those finely toned arms and broad, muscular shoulders. I'm sure they'll serve you well at this position.
Oh, is that right?
May I ask a question? I know you're looking for a secretary, but is there a manual labor aspect to the job?
It says here, word for word: "I like to get my balls rubbed at massage parlors. Aww yeah." Is this some kind of joke?

Just thought I'd throw a little humor in there. But yeah,
it's true. It's actually part of my job⑬fieldwork, so to
speak. You know how we Japanese mix business with pleasure.
That's quite an astute observation. Now bear in mind, while I am looking for a secretary, the purpose of this interview is not to evaluate your job skills.
I'm trying to see what sort of person you are... to see if I like you. My decision making is simply a matter of taste.
That's right⑬I remember the job called for a brawny build and a cheerful personality. The personality part, I get. But why brawny?

I mean, I understand you're looking for a secretary,
but is there a manual labor aspect to the job?

It says: "I've got balls of steel AND exceptional brawn."
Since you went out of your way to write that, and even used
all caps, I assume you're very confident in that regard?

Oh, absolutely. There's not much I'm proud of in my life,
but one thing I can take pride in is my strength.
I intend to explain that later. Why, are you worried over what this job entails?
Oh, no, not at all! Whatever the job, I'll trust your judgment and do what needs to be done!
Spoken like a true man. I will also put my trust in you, among other things.
Then I'll do my best to never betray that trust!
(That said, is this really a secretary job...?)
Honestly, I am a little concerned whether I measure up to the job or not.

Let me do the measuring here. I assume that, by virtue of
you being here, you already trust my judgment?
Yes, of course! Didn't mean to doubt you, sir!

Isn't that a little... patronizing? This is a job interview,
so naturally I'd be at least a little curious about the
details.

Your reaction is perfectly warranted. But, there are some
security precautions I need to take, so I ask that you be
compliant with the process. That is, if you're comfortable.
Oh, of course. I didn't know. My apologies.
Now, as you can probably guess, I founded this company and I make all the decisions.
I handle the hiring process by myself. I interview all the candidates. And I alone make the call whether to hire or not.
With this kind of organizational structure, I expect absolute loyalty from my workers. It's a relationship like that of a father and his sons.
Let me ask you this⑬Shinada, can you obey me like you would your father? Are you mentally, physically, emotionally prepared to do my every bidding, no matter how excruciating?
(Whoa, this sounds like the yakuza. Is this company a front for mobsters?)
This could be your last chance to turn back. Well? Can you swear total subservience to me?
I can't swear to that.
I see. But think carefully about this opportunity. I'll give you another chance. Shinada, will you swear total subservience to me?
Yes! I swear to it.

Excellent. That took courage. Then, Shinada, allow me to
congratulate you! Welcome to our corporate family.
Huh? Just like that?
I told you⑬I make the decisions. If I say go, there's no one to say no. My decision is final.
Oh, and don't worry about the salary. I can assure you, we're far more generous than Nightlife Magazine. Our pockets run deep for a reason!
(Seriously? Something feels off about this...)
All right, Shinada. You're my secretary now. Let's get you started right away.
Uh... Okay. What should I do?
Haha, come with me and see for yourself.
You're a rebellious lad, all right. No wonder you caught my eye. You're welcome back here if you ever change your mind, Shinada-kun.
Not happening!
Okay, then. Here's your severance pay. I trust you'll keep this dark secret between us... like any good father and son.
You got <Color:8>30,000 yen<Color:Default>.
(Geez. So much for trying to change careers...)
You got 1,900 experience points.
What on earth is going on here!?
Oh, you know. Just another day at the office. You'll get used to it.
Get used to my boss wearing nothing but a loincloth!? Fat chance!

Oh, don't get your fundoshi in a bunch. Now strip, Shinada.
You swore total subservience, remember? Like a son to his
father. So, come on over to daddy! No need to be shy!
So this is what you were planning!? Don't you find it wrong to just spring this on me out of nowhere?
Oh, believe me, I do. In fact, that's the thrill of it. The mere thought of how bizarre the situation is makes my heart throb, among other things!

Now savor it, Shinada. Breathe it all in. I've been waiting
for this moment since the first time I laid eyes on you.
And what a feast you are!
So... So that interview was all just for show? We'd have ended up here either way?
That's right, Shinada. And now it's time for you to end up on my lap. Do as you're told, my son! Or daddy's gonna have to spank you!

No one's spanking anyone today! You can forget about the
roleplay⑬I'm going home!
Heheh. You just keep getting better and better. I knew I had you pegged as the perfect <Italic>wayward son</Italic>. Father knows best, after all.

But I can see you have a wild streak that requires a bit of
discipline. As your father, I hate to do this, but you'll
thank me for it in the end. Get ready for some tough love!

What the hell is with this company!? Do all your employees
get initiated like this!? You know what⑬I don't even care.
Let's just get this over with.
Okay, okay! You win! Please... stop the violence! I'll give you your refund!
Damn straight you will! And make it snappy!
You got <Color:8>4,500 yen<Color:Default>.

You know... I'm sad. You were the first customer we had in
such a long time.
Well, get some better looking girls at least. Nobody would go for cheap but horrible.
What a terrible thing to say. Yuka-chan and Rumi-chan are solid eights in my book, even low nines.
What, on a scale of a hundred? You are not cut out for this job, bud.
Aww...
You got 3,600 experience points.

Hello, and welcome to the Cheeky Chestnut: the hottest, most
happening massage parlor in all of Kineicho! For a little
stress relief now, there's always a happy ending later!
For an incredibly low, fixed price of 4,500 yen, our girls go the distance for no extra pay. That's my personal guarantee!
Eh, maybe some other time. I'm pretty broke as it is.
Ooh, too bad! But hey, we'll be here!
Say no more, my good man. I will avail myself of your services.
You handed over <Color:8>4,500 yen<Color:Default>.
Ah, yes indeed! Avail away, kind sir! Booking for one, right this way!

Come on, chief, that's just cold. You're really gonna walk
on by without even so much as a glance?
Um. What?

Step inside and discover a world full of wonder! Mystery!
Excitement! Our massage parlor guarantees a happy ending
with every purchase⑬it's the happiest ending on Earth!

We're the Cheeky Chestnut, and for the incredibly low price
of 4,500 yen, our girls go the extra distance for none of
the extra pay!
Huh, that is cheap. But I've never heard of this place before.

Well, we opened only recently. But I can guarantee our girls
will not only give you a happy ending⑬they'll give you a
new beginning! It could very well transform your life!
(I guess I can use this for a story if worse comes to worst.)
